title: 🍋 The Lemonade Empire
theme: Build a thriving lemonade business from Grandma's recipe
description: You've inherited your grandmother's legendary lemonade recipe and 500 Mento Coins. Turn this summer into a business success story through smart decisions about location, pricing, inventory, and competition. Learn entrepreneurship fundamentals through hands-on experience!

how_to_play.title: How to Play
steps: Read each business scenario about running your lemonade stand
Make decisions about location, pricing, inventory, and how to handle competition
Watch how your choices affect Mento Coins, Reputation, and Daily Sales
Manage your resources carefully -- running out of inventory or cash means lost customers
Grow your lemonade stand into an empire by making smart entrepreneurial choices each round
tips: Balance price and quality -- too cheap and you lose money, too expensive and customers leave
Keep an eye on your Reputation score -- it drives long-term customer loyalty
Invest in creativity and financial skills early to unlock better business options later

learning_objectives: Apply fundamental entrepreneurship concepts including location selection, pricing strategy, inventory management, and customer acquisition
Analyze competitive threats and develop strategic responses such as differentiation, collaboration, or niche positioning
Practice financial decision-making by balancing revenue, costs, and investment to grow a small business sustainably
Understand market dynamics including supply and demand, weather impacts on sales, and the role of reputation in customer loyalty
Develop creative problem-solving skills when facing business challenges like new competitors, supply shortages, and scaling decisions

player_profile.name: Young Entrepreneur
player_profile.goal: Build a successful lemonade business and learn entrepreneurship
player_profile.background: A young person with Grandma's famous lemonade recipe and big dreams

rounds.title: Round 1: Location Decision
rounds.story:
It's the first day of summer! You have Grandma's legendary lemonade recipe and {{mento_coins}} Mento Coins to start your business.

Your mom gives you three location options. Each has different advantages:
• Front yard: Safe and free, but limited foot traffic
• Local park: Busy but requires expensive permit
• Partner location: Share space at friend's family store

Where you set up will determine how many potential customers you reach.
rounds.setting: Your neighborhood on a sunny summer morning

choices.label: Front Yard (Safe & Free)
choices.description: Set up in your own front yard. No costs, no permits needed. Safe and comfortable, but only 20-30 neighbors will pass by daily. Limited growth potential but zero risk.
choices.feedback: You set up a colorful table in your front yard. Mrs. Chen from next door becomes your first customer! It's comfortable and safe, but you wonder if you're limiting your potential.
choices.narrative_outcome: Your immediate neighbors support you, but foot traffic is limited. By lunch, you've served 8 people - mostly people you already knew.
choices.counterfactual_feedback: You set up a colorful table in your front yard. Mrs.

choices.label: Local Park (Permit: 150 MC)
choices.description: Rent a spot at the busiest park in town. Costs 150 Mento Coins for a vendor permit, but hundreds of people visit daily. High upfront investment with strong growth potential.
choices.feedback: After getting your permit, you set up near the playground. Within an hour, you have your first line of customers! The park is buzzing with activity.
choices.narrative_outcome: Families, joggers, and kids playing everywhere. The permit was expensive, but you're surrounded by potential customers. You feel the energy of a real marketplace!
choices.counterfactual_feedback: After getting your permit, you set up near the playground. Within an hour, you have your first line of customers! The park is buzzing with activity.

choices.label: Partner with Friend's Store (50 MC/week)
choices.description: Set up outside your friend Maria's family convenience store. Pay 50 Mento Coins per week. They'll recommend you to their regular customers. Partnership approach with moderate investment.
choices.feedback: Maria is excited! Her mom puts a sign in the store window. You decorate the stand together, and the store's regular customers are curious and friendly.
choices.narrative_outcome: The store gets steady traffic - especially during lunch and after school. Mrs. Lopez promises to bring her book club next week. You're learning that relationships matter in business!

rounds.image_prompt: a bright front yard with a lemonade stand under a colorful umbrella, surrounded by blooming flowers and a sunny blue sky, a cozy and inviting atmosphere with a few curious neighbors nearby
rounds.coaching_moment: Consider how this choice affects your long-term resources, not just the immediate gain.
rounds.reflection_prompt: What tradeoff did this decision reveal? What did you gain, and what did you give up?

expert_pick.reason: The most effective leaders adapt their approach based on the situation — not habit.

rounds.title: Round 1: Inventory Purchase
rounds.story:
Your location is set! Now you need supplies. You have {{mento_coins}} Mento Coins remaining.

Grandma's recipe makes lemonade in batches:
• Small batch: 30 cups for 50 MC (1.67 MC per cup)
• Medium batch: 80 cups for 120 MC (1.50 MC per cup) - bulk discount!
• Large batch: 150 cups for 200 MC (1.33 MC per cup) - best rate!

Fresh lemonade lasts about 2 days. How much will you invest?
rounds.goal: Balance inventory investment with available capital
rounds.setting: Grocery store - time to buy ingredients

choices.label: Small Batch (50 MC → 30 cups)
choices.description: Conservative approach. Low risk of waste since lemonade spoils in 2 days. You might run out during busy times, but you won't lose much if sales are slow.
choices.feedback: You buy fresh lemons and carefully prepare 30 cups following Grandma's recipe. The kitchen smells amazing! It's manageable, but you wonder if you should have bought more.
choices.counterfactual_feedback: You buy fresh lemons and carefully prepare 30 cups following Grandma's recipe. The kitchen smells amazing! It's manageable, but you wonder if you should have bought more.

choices.label: Medium Batch (120 MC → 80 cups)
choices.description: Balanced approach with small bulk discount. Cost per cup drops to 1.50 MC. Enough to handle decent traffic without massive waste risk. Smart business planning.
choices.feedback: The grocery clerk notices your purchase and asks about your business - you explain and she's impressed! You spend 3 hours preparing. The math feels good - lower cost per cup means better profits.
choices.counterfactual_feedback: The grocery clerk notices your purchase and asks about your business - you explain and she's impressed! You spend 3 hours preparing. The math feels good - lower cost per cup means better profits.

choices.label: Large Batch (200 MC → 150 cups)
choices.description: Aggressive investment! Best bulk rate at 1.33 MC per cup. You're investing 40% of starting capital. If you sell out, your margins are excellent. If not, you'll waste product and money.
choices.feedback: You buy in bulk at the wholesale club! The cashier jokes you're starting a lemonade factory. Your kitchen becomes a production facility. 150 cups ready - you're all in now!

rounds.image_prompt: a vibrant marketplace filled with colorful stalls, banners waving, a group of eager customers examining a large display of lemonade ingredients, bright sunshine illuminating the scene
rounds.coaching_moment: Think about trade-offs: what are you giving up to get this benefit?

expert_pick.reason: The most effective leaders adapt their approach based on the situation — not habit.

rounds.title: Round 1: Pricing Strategy
rounds.story:
Everything is ready! You have {{inventory}} cups of lemonade and {{mento_coins}} Mento Coins.

Now the crucial decision: PRICE PER CUP

Market research shows:
• Most stands charge 10-12 MC
• Premium stands charge 15-18 MC
• Budget options charge 8-9 MC

Your cost per cup depends on batch size. How will you position yourself?
rounds.goal: Set competitive pricing to maximize profit and volume
rounds.setting: Your lemonade stand - opening in 10 minutes!

choices.label: Budget Pricing (8 MC/cup)
choices.description: Price below market to attract volume. Parents and kids will appreciate the value. You'll sell more cups but margins are thin. Need high volume to succeed.

calc._COMMENT: Will calculate profit based on inventory sold

choices.feedback: You make a big sign: 'JUST 8 MENTO COINS!' Kids are excited - most stands charge more. Word spreads quickly. You're the 'value brand'!
choices.counterfactual_feedback: You make a big sign: 'JUST 8 MENTO COINS!' Kids are excited - most stands charge more. Word spreads quickly.

choices.label: Market Pricing (12 MC/cup)
choices.description: Standard market rate - what customers expect to pay. Balanced approach between volume and margin. You won't scare customers away, and you're making healthy profit per cup.
choices.feedback: You price it at 12 Mento Coins - same as other quality stands. Customers don't hesitate. They're used to this price. Professional and fair positioning!
choices.counterfactual_feedback: You price it at 12 Mento Coins - same as other quality stands. Customers don't hesitate.

choices.label: Premium Pricing (18 MC/cup)
choices.description: Above market rate as premium product. Grandma's award-winning recipe justifies the price! You'll sell fewer cups but make much more per sale. Quality positioning strategy.
choices.feedback: Your sign reads: 'Grandma's Original Recipe - County Fair Champion - Premium Quality!' Some hesitate at the price, but those who try it say 'WOW! This IS special!'
choices.counterfactual_feedback: Your sign reads: 'Grandma's Original Recipe - County Fair Champion - Premium Quality!' Some hesitate at the price, but those who try it say 'WOW! This IS special!'.

choices.label: Dynamic Pricing (10-15 MC)
choices.description: Variable pricing! Morning: 10 MC, Peak hot hours (12-3pm): 15 MC, Evening: 12 MC. Like airlines or Uber. Sophisticated but requires explanation to customers.
choices.feedback: You create a pricing board showing different times. Some customers are confused, but you explain demand-based pricing. Most think it's clever! You feel like a real entrepreneur!

rounds.image_prompt: a vibrant lemonade stand at a bustling park under a bright blue sky, colorful cups of lemonade neatly arranged, excited customers discussing prices, a cheerful atmosphere
rounds.coaching_moment: How might your team react to this decision? What about your customers?
rounds.reflection_prompt: Why did you choose this option? What were you trying to protect or grow?

expert_pick.reason: Resilience research shows that processing setbacks openly builds stronger teams.

rounds.title: Round 2: Weather Crisis
rounds.story:
Opening day is going great! You've made some sales ({{daily_sales}} cups sold) and customers love the lemonade.

Then at 2 PM, dark clouds roll in. Weather app shows 90% chance of thunderstorms within the hour. You still have {{inventory}} cups of inventory.

What's your move?

choices.label: Pack Up Immediately
choices.description: Close early and save your inventory. Minimize losses but disappoint customers who wanted afternoon lemonade. Conservative crisis response.
choices.feedback: You quickly pack everything. Some customers look disappointed. Your inventory is safe, but you've lost potential afternoon sales.
choices.counterfactual_feedback: You quickly pack everything. Some customers look disappointed.

choices.label: Storm Special - Discount!
choices.description: Stay open with 'Before the Storm' discount pricing. Sell remaining inventory quickly at reduced price before rain hits. Turn crisis into opportunity!
choices.feedback: You announce a 'Storm's Coming Special!' People rushing home stop to grab a quick cup. You're turning crisis into opportunity!
choices.counterfactual_feedback: You announce a 'Storm's Coming Special!' People rushing home stop to grab a quick cup. You're turning crisis into opportunity!.

choices.label: Add Hot Chocolate (Cost: 80 MC)
choices.description: Pivot to hot drinks! Quickly prepare hot chocolate for rainy weather sales. Creative problem-solving but requires investment and speed.
choices.feedback: Brilliant! You remember you have chocolate at home. When rain starts, you're the ONLY stand with hot drinks. Customers are amazed by your quick thinking!

choices.label: Negotiate Indoor Space (30 MC tip)
choices.description: Ask nearby shops if you can set up inside temporarily. Costs 30 MC tip to shop owner. Creative problem-solving and negotiation skills.
choices.feedback: You approach a nearby bookstore. The owner is impressed by your initiative and lets you set up by the entrance. You continue selling while staying dry!
choices.counterfactual_feedback: You approach a nearby bookstore. The owner is impressed by your initiative and lets you set up by the entrance.

rounds.image_prompt: a vibrant lemonade stand on a bustling street, customers smiling with cups in hand, suddenly overshadowed by dark, ominous clouds rolling in, lightning flickering in the distance
rounds.coaching_moment: Look at your current resource levels — which constraint are you trying to address?

expert_pick.reason: The most effective leaders adapt their approach based on the situation — not habit.

rounds.title: Round 2: Customer Complaint
rounds.story:
The storm has passed. Business continues.

Then a customer returns looking upset. 'This lemonade is too sour! I want a refund!' They paid {{price_per_cup}} MC.

This is your first complaint. Your reputation is {{reputation}}. How you handle this will matter.

choices.label: Refuse Refund - Defend Recipe
choices.description: Explain that's how the recipe is supposed to taste. Grandma won the county fair with this exact recipe! No refund given.
choices.feedback: The customer leaves angry and tells their friends. You saved the money but damaged your reputation. Sometimes being 'right' isn't worth it.
choices.counterfactual_feedback: The customer leaves angry and tells their friends. You saved the money but damaged your reputation.

choices.label: Issue Refund Immediately
choices.description: Give money back, no questions asked. Customer service first. You'll take the loss to maintain good reputation.
choices.feedback: The customer is surprised by your professionalism. They thank you and actually come back the next day to try it again! Word spreads about your great service.
choices.counterfactual_feedback: The customer is surprised by your professionalism. They thank you and actually come back the next day to try it again! Word spreads about your great service.

choices.label: Refund + Customize Recipe
choices.description: Refund AND offer to make a custom batch with less lemon just for them. Show you truly care about customer satisfaction.
choices.feedback: You refund them AND make a custom batch right there! They're blown away by your service. They post about you on social media. You've created a loyal fan!

choices.label: Gather Feedback & Improve
choices.description: Refund them and ask detailed questions. Use this as learning opportunity to potentially improve your product based on customer input.
choices.feedback: You turn this into learning! You ask what would make it perfect. You realize offering slight customization could be your competitive advantage.
choices.counterfactual_feedback: You turn this into learning! You ask what would make it perfect. You realize offering slight customization could be your competitive advantage.

rounds.image_prompt: a bright lemonade stand on a sunny street, colorful cups stacked high, a customer with a frown holding a half-full cup, vibrant flowers swaying in the gentle breeze
rounds.coaching_moment: Sometimes the bold choice carries risk, but also the highest reward. Weigh carefully.
rounds.reflection_prompt: How might the people affected by this choice experience the outcome?

expert_pick.reason: The most effective leaders adapt their approach based on the situation — not habit.

rounds.title: Round 3: Growth Decision
rounds.setting: Your successful stand - time to scale

choices.label: Open Second Location (200 MC)
choices.description: Your friend from another neighborhood wants to use your recipe! Franchise model: You invest 200 MC to help them start, you get 30% of their profits ongoing.
choices.feedback: You're expanding! You spend a weekend training your friend. You're building a small empire through smart delegation!
choices.counterfactual_feedback: You're expanding! You spend a weekend training your friend. You're building a small empire through smart delegation!.

choices.label: Upgrade to Premium (250 MC)
choices.description: Invest in organic lemons, custom branded cups, professional signage. Position as premium brand. Quality over quantity strategy.
choices.feedback: You invest in perfection! Organic ingredients, beautiful branding. Customers notice immediately. You're not just selling lemonade - you're selling an experience.
choices.counterfactual_feedback: You invest in perfection! Organic ingredients, beautiful branding. Customers notice immediately.

choices.label: Add New Flavors (150 MC)
choices.description: Develop 3 new flavors: strawberry, mint, and mango lemonade. Product diversification strategy. Cater to more tastes.
choices.feedback: You experiment with new flavors! Some work better than others, but customers love having choices. Your stand becomes the most interesting in town!

choices.label: Build Loyalty Program (100 MC)
choices.description: Create punch cards, customer database, rewards. Focus on retention over acquisition. 'Buy 5, get 1 free' program.
choices.feedback: You launch 'Lemon Lovers Club!' Customers love it. You start learning names and preferences. Building community, not just customers!
choices.counterfactual_feedback: You launch 'Lemon Lovers Club!' Customers love it. You start learning names and preferences.

glossary_terms.definition: The process of ordering, storing, and using a company's inventory - including raw materials, components, and finished products. Good inventory management prevents waste while ensuring you have enough to meet demand.
glossary_terms.example: Buying 150 cups of lemonade at once gets you a bulk discount, but if they spoil before you sell them, you've wasted money.

glossary_terms.definition: How a business sets prices for products or services. Prices can be set based on costs, competition, perceived value, or market positioning.
glossary_terms.example: Charging 18 MC for premium lemonade versus 8 MC for budget lemonade - same product, different market positioning.

glossary_terms.definition: The support and assistance provided to customers before, during, and after a purchase. Good customer service builds loyalty and reputation.
glossary_terms.example: Offering a refund and custom-made lemonade to an unhappy customer turns a complaint into a loyal fan.

glossary_terms.definition: The point where total revenue equals total costs. After this point, you start making profit.
glossary_terms.example: If each cup costs 1.50 MC to make and you sell it for 12 MC, you need to sell enough cups to cover your 200 MC initial investment.

glossary_terms.definition: How a business wants to be perceived by customers relative to competitors. Positions can be: budget, mid-market, or premium.
glossary_terms.example: Choosing between being the 'affordable option', 'same as others', or 'premium quality' lemonade stand.

Pivots fast when conditions change instead of waiting them out
Differentiates on something real, not just lower price
Communicates price changes honestly to regulars instead of sneaking them
Reinvests winnings into the next experiment, not into bigger spending
Discounts as the first lever for any problem
Waits for conditions to improve instead of changing the offering
Competes on price against someone with deeper pockets
Hides cost increases hoping customers don't notice
